title: HW↔BIZ-001: BOM Cost vs. Target + Volume Forecast vs. Component Availability
description: The Hardware Engineer provides a detailed BOM (Bill of Materials) with component costs and vendor sources, NRE (Non-Recurring Engineering) cost estimates (tooling, test fixtures, mold tooling), prototype/production lead-time estimates, and certification-testing cost/schedule estimates; the Business Consultant provides the target BOM cost ceiling per market segment and pricing strategy, second-sourcing requirements driven by supply-chain-risk policy, and volume forecasts for procurement planning. Grounded in HARDWARE_ENGINEER_SKILL §6.9 and BUSINESS_CONSULTANT_SKILL §6.3. A BOM that exceeds the business cost ceiling is a cost-material deviation: it must be raised as an ADR (with a Business Impact Assessment), never silently traded.

hardware_cost_package.description: HW→BIZ: detailed BOM, NRE, lead times, certification costs, and ceiling reconciliation.

bom_vs_ceiling.description: Reconciliation of bom_total against the BIZ-supplied ceiling.

exceedance_adr_ref.description: Required when within_ceiling = false (cost-material deviation → ADR + BIA).

business_targets.description: BIZ→HW: cost ceiling, second-sourcing policy, volume forecast.

x-macp.tier_rationale: Routine BOM-cost / volume-forecast exchange at feasibility, design freeze, and ramp-up is agent-autonomous. A BOM exceedance over the business ceiling is cost-material and escalates to an ADR + Business Impact Assessment (not a silent trade).
x-macp.cadence: TRIGGER (at product feasibility stage; at design freeze; at manufacturing ramp-up decision)
confirm_conditions: the detailed BOM and bom_total carry currency and (for the total) an explicit unit; every component cost carries a currency
lead times and certification schedule carry explicit units
bom_vs_ceiling.within_ceiling is reported honestly against the BIZ ceiling
second-sourcing is reflected where BIZ supply-chain policy requires it
reject_conditions: a BOM over the BIZ ceiling presented as acceptable without an exceedance ADR (silent cost trade — Never Silently Deviate)
a cost or lead-time figure emitted without a currency/unit (units rule §3.10)
a single-sourced critical component presented as compliant where BIZ mandates a second source
counter_conditions: a cost ceiling supplied without a market segment — request the segment/pricing context before reconciling the BOM
a volume forecast missing its period — request the procurement horizon before committing lead times
